r0.why: 1096-1099, first of wars initiated/supported/directed by Latin Church (1); aim to return Holy Land after Rashidun 7th-c conquest (2); Muslim rule for hundreds of years (3); Jerusalem captured July 1099 (16); four Crusader states (19)

r1.why: Seljuk practices threatened local Christians, pilgrims, Byzantium (3); Alexios I envoys to Piacenza 1095 vs Seljuk-led Turks (4); Urban II at Clermont backed request, urged armed pilgrimage (5)

r2.why: Enthusiastic response across all classes (6); thousands of mostly poor led by French priest Peter the Hermit (7); anti-Jewish activity incl. Rhineland massacres in Germany (8); annihilated in Kilij Arslan's ambush at Civetot Oct 1096 after leaving Byzantine Anatolia (9)

r3.why: High nobility left late summer 1096, reached Constantinople Nov-Apr (10); up to 100,000 incl. non-combatants (11); Nicaea June 1097 with Byzantine naval assault (13); Dorylaeum July vs mounted archers (14); difficult march, Antioch taken June 1098 (15)

r4.why: Fatimid Jerusalem reached June 1099, stormed 15 July with large fraction massacred (16); Ascalon repulse ended crusade (17); most returned home (18); presence until loss of last major stronghold at Acre 1291 (20)

r5.why: Population grew greatly by 11th c (30); Church dominant influence (31); feudalism: military service for right to rent from lands (32); Byzantine need coincided with warriors' willingness to accept papal command (29); holy war doctrine from Augustine (40) and his conditions (41)
